correctness.rationale: I reconstructed the icosahedral graph from exact golden-ratio coordinates and verified the given two-ring labeling, then enumerated all 125 perfect matchings by unique first-edge recursion. In an independent coefficient calculation, for each matching M and each subset S of it, contracting S and deleting M minus S counts exactly the trees with T intersect M=S. Summing by |S| gives the coefficients, with parallel edges retained. Grounded Laplacian determinants modulo the prime 2147483647 are exact counts since the total edge-subset bound is 2^30. The run /workspace/branches/check2.py recovers all five factorizations and multiplicities. It verifies the common value 5184000 and derivative 11404800 at t=1 and divides the adjacent differences by (t-1)^2, leaving coefficient vectors (6876,16158,14052,5358,756), (9500,20330,15906,5422,682), (8968,15480,9914,2788,290), (5376,9472,6208,1792,192). These exact coefficients prove the strict order on the entire stated domain except 1, where all matchings tie; this is not a sample of parameter values. The symmetric difference of two perfect matchings is a union of disjoint even cycles, so size four is exactly a single alternating four-cycle flip. The independently enumerated flip-isolated matchings are exactly the P5 class.
residual_risks: The order is for product conductance weights on the specified graph and six-edge perfect matchings, not minimum additive cost, other graph families, arbitrary marked sets, or individual edge weights.

evidence: The matrix-tree and determinant lemma give a general evaluation method; the specialized graph families inspected do not include marked icosahedral perfect matchings. General graph-design work includes weighted tree objectives and matroid constraints or approximation guarantees rather than the exact six-edge products and all-contrast ordering here.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General formulas and algorithms credit the method and let one compute the numbers, but do not evaluate equality, distinguish the five specific polynomials, or certify an order throughout both t regimes without instance-specific work.

evidence: All 120 verified icosahedral automorphisms give five matching orbits of sizes 5,20,60,30,10, each one polynomial class. An automorphism preserves the iid arrival law and maps terminal matchings equivariantly, so its five distinct kinetic probability classes are exactly those orbits as well. Across the same classes the exact kinetic probabilities order 30>10>60>20>5, whereas the weighted-tree order is 5>20>60>30>10 away from t=1.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Orbit invariance gives an upper bound of five classes, and the known frozen set identifies one orbit, but that alone does not make all five polynomials distinct or make the frozen set an optimizer; the alternate invariant's opposite preference emphasizes the difference. The uniform count fixes only the common specialization, and the product-weight ranking has to be proved separately.

evidence: The flip record identifies the exact five isolated matchings, and the matching-complex record counts 125 perfect matchings. The dimer adsorption orbit partition agrees by the invariant crosswalk. The planar tree/dimer bijection uses an auxiliary graph, and the constrained-tree paper asks for minimum-weight trees containing a matching, not trees generating the full intersection-size distribution of a prescribed matching.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The partition is genuine overlap, but the kinetic ranking disagrees and the auxiliary-graph and constrained-tree properties are not equivalent to this marked-edge generating function. Even the total for trees containing a prescribed matching is just the coefficient of t^6.

originality.rationale: The matching count, flip-isolated class and uniform tree baseline are known. The same-day adsorption work gives the same five classes as a partition of matchings, not just the same size multiset: the independent automorphism check finds a single graph-automorphism orbit in each polynomial class, and the adsorption probabilities are automorphism-invariant and take five distinct values. The adsorption ranking, however, is 30>10>60>20>5 by multiplicity label, in particular putting the tree-maximizing orbit last. The distinct finding is the five evaluated tree polynomials and their strict, contrast-independent ranking, not discovery of the orbit partition or of the isolated matchings. No same-day publication order is inferred.
residual_risks: No exhaustive priority claim; unindexed equivalent coefficient or transfer-spectrum tables could exist. The related polygonal-chain paper was unavailable for detailed comparison. Same-day dates do not establish order.

value.rationale: The graph, the all-vertices disjoint marking constraint and the spanning-tree partition function are natural independently of the resulting finite table. It is structurally useful that the full family has one strict order for both weakening and strengthening, with exactly the known flip-isolated orbit winning, unlike the adsorption weights on the same orbits. The evaluated polynomials provide full intersection-count statistics and a reproducible benchmark for network-design and tree-ensemble comparisons, not merely a count of matching types already known.
residual_risks: No support for a general optimality principle on other graphs or for dynamic selection by a tree-weighting mechanism.
